analysis:
This PR changes one documentation line in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (line 2183, a config table row). The change clarifies that a non-empty `[backend] enabled_models` also bounds coordinator model commands and rollouts, and links the operator filter in the configuration reference. The supplied units are base-side excerpts of the same file (lines 1227-2134). The changed line 2183 is outside the supplied excerpt range, so I could only check it through the patch hunk. The surrounding text covers stop, restart, status, doctor, models, update, logout and report behavior. None of that is modified.

No code, endpoint, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache behavior changes. No threat-model assumption is invalidated. The new text describes a restrictive control: the operator's local model filter limits what coordinator-driven model commands and rollouts can do. That narrows coordinator-driven model changes and does not widen attack surface. Related threats are T-012, A-004 and TB-002, and nothing in the text weakens them.

Open integration question: whether the code actually enforces the filter on coordinator model commands and rollouts, as the doc now says, is outside the supplied evidence. The target section (../reference/configuration.md#provider-model-selection) and the enforcing Swift sources are also not supplied. This is a documentation-accuracy matter and is not claimed as a vulnerability. No findings.
